questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The positive associations I had to Belgium. I have only heard good things about Belgien people and Belgium as a whole and for that reason I wanted to explore it more.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The information is relatively easy to find. Though it can be a bit difficult to figure out exactly which information you need when, but I had few difficulties finding the relevant document/links when I knew which one I was looking for.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We participated in a lecture/information class on where to find relevant links/documents and where to ask for additional help.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Housing is somewhat available, but it can be a frustrating experience to find housing when living in a different country. 

Still I suggest gaining access to facebook groups for housing in Leuven. Try to write people who post or make a post about yourself.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Leuven is a small city and for that reason it does not make a big difference if you live on campus or not.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You look for the classes you want and are available for you to take  on a website. Then you enroll in them on the online student platform.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The proces was covered in the introduction and information lecture in the first week. Additionally you have the option of going to a class before commmitting further to it.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Some courses had different requirements than were stated on the website for example some courses were only for students with a specific degree in KU leuven. Other than this very succesful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try out a lecture with the professor before committing to the course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I only took master courses. These were of similar or slightly lower difficulty than what I have been used to at Copenhagen University.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching is rather similar to that of UCPH. KU Leuven similarly used group work, individual work and lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Global politics and Diplomacy
Public Affairs
EU Trade Policy 
Human Computer Interaction 
China and Global Politics
North Africa, the Middle East and Euro-Mediterranean Relations

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would highly suggest taking the public affairs and global politics courses. The professors are both great and the courses provide highly relevant knowledge for our studies.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I ended up going out to eat a lot more than I expected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Most things are a bit cheaper than in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sportwise they have a Gym with a special student discount and they have sports offers for pretty much anything you can imagine every week. The European student network (ESN) and other organizations create a lot of different events which you join. There is a huge variation in these events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend trying out a cantus and a bunch of the things organized by ESN Leuven.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend going to Brussels, Brugge, Ghent and Namur on trips.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The culture is pretty similar to the Danish one so it is not much of an issue.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to befriend the ESN people since they are often more local and have bigger local networks.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The Belgium students go home on the weekends.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: It's difficult to pinpoint one thing, maybe their beer culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Participate in things, be open to new ideas and explore

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I reccomend living in Leuven or Heverlee rather than pendling from a different city since the trains stop going around 00:00. Also it is not a big issue to live outside of the "ring"

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a bunch of new people with different backgrounds and experiencing a lot of new things.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: All the practicalities before and at the start of the semester eg. find a place to stay, do the paper work for both universities, make sure you have the equipment to comfortably stay and live in your room.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
